violated_contract: When one step combines several sources into one sequence and a later step must find each source's items in it, the later step must use the layout the combining step actually produced. Re-deriving positions from source order (source k's items as one block after source k-1's) breaks as soon as the combining step sorts or interleaves. A consumer that validates the assumed positions then rejects valid work, and one that does not validate binds data to another source's item.
canonical_prevention: The combining step returns an explicit position map with the combined sequence, and the consumer checks and moves data through that map, never through running offsets. A behavioural test feeds interleaving sources through the real producer and the real consumer and asserts the moved data lands on the right item.
